itinerary.title: Kodachadri Trek – Altitude: 4,403 ft | Distance: 13 km Early morning arrival at the homestay near Sampekatte.
itinerary.description: Freshen up, have a hot breakfast, collect packed lunch, and head to the forest checkpost to begin the trek. Trail Progression: Base village through paddy fields and jungle entry (~2 km, 1 hour) — the trail opens immediately into forest after the checkpost Dense forest ascent to Kumble Village (~3 km, 1.5 hours) — steady uphill through thick canopy with multiple stream crossings Hidlumane Waterfalls (~1 km) — the trail passes directly through the falls; stop for refreshments (buttermilk and lemon juice available), photographs, and a short rest before continuing Forest and grassland ascent to the summit ridge (~4 km, 2 hours) — the forest gives way to open rolling grasslands as you approach the top Kodachadri Peak (4,403 ft) — summit with panoramic views of the Arabian Sea, Sharavathi Backwaters, and the Western Ghats. The Sarvajna Peetha and Mookambika Devi temple are at the top. Packed lunch at the summit. Descent: Jeep ride from the summit back to the homestay — a thrilling bumpy ride through the forest jeep trail, saving both time and energy. Return to homestay by evening. Hot snacks, dinner, bonfire (weather permitting), overnight rest. Overnight: Homestay near Sampekatte, Shimoga District. Day 2 Nagara Fort → Sakrebailu Elephant Camp → Return to Bangalore Morning at the homestay — early exploration of the local surroundings and plantation walks before a hot breakfast and checkout. Nagara Fort: A 16th-century hilltop fort built by the Keladi Nayaka rulers — ruins with historical significance and views of the surrounding Malnad countryside. A 30-minute stop worth every minute. Sakrebailu Elephant Camp: Located on the banks of the Tunga River near Shimoga, this elephant camp is one of the finest in Karnataka. Watch elephants being bathed and fed in their natural surroundings. Entry fee is self-sponsored. Self-sponsored lunch en route. Reach Bangalore by 10:00 PM – 11:00 PM depending on traffic. Note: Drop points are the same as pickup locations. Travel time may vary based on road conditions.

faqs.question: What is the Kodachadri Trek?
faqs.answer: The Kodachadri Trek is a 13 km trail to the 10th highest peak in Karnataka at 4,403 ft (1,342 m), located inside Mookambika Wildlife Sanctuary in Shimoga district. The trail passes through Hidlumane Waterfalls mid-route and ends at a summit with views of the Arabian Sea and Sharavathi Backwaters.

faqs.question: How long is the Kodachadri Trek?
faqs.answer: The Kodachadri Trek is 13 km. The ascent takes 4–5 hours and the descent is done by jeep. Total time on Day 1 is approximately 7–8 hours including breaks.

faqs.question: What is the altitude of Kodachadri Peak?
faqs.answer: Kodachadri Peak stands at 4,403 ft (1,342 m). It is the 10th highest peak in Karnataka and a Government of Karnataka designated Natural Heritage Site.

faqs.question: What is the difficulty level of Kodachadri Trek?
faqs.answer: Moderate. The trail has steep inclines, rocky paths, stream crossings, and the Hidlumane Falls crossing. Prior trekking experience is desirable but not mandatory. Good fitness is required.

faqs.question: Is Kodachadri Trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes, with decent fitness. Beginners who exercise regularly and can walk 6–8 km comfortably can complete this trek with the support of a guide. The jeep descent removes the most strenuous part of the return journey.

faqs.question: What is the best time for Kodachadri Trek?
faqs.answer: September to February. Post-monsoon (September–October) brings Hidlumane Falls at near-full flow and lush forest. November to February offers cool weather and clear Arabian Sea views from the summit.

faqs.question: Can you see the Arabian Sea from Kodachadri?
faqs.answer: Yes. On a clear day, the Arabian Sea is clearly visible from the Kodachadri Peak summit — especially during sunset. This is one of the very few Western Ghats peaks from which the sea is visible.

faqs.question: What is the significance of Sarvajna Peetha at Kodachadri?
faqs.answer: The Sarvajna Peetha is a historic throne at the Kodachadri summit believed to be where Adi Shankara, the 8th-century Vedic philosopher, meditated and was granted omniscience. A small Mookambika Devi temple also stands at the summit, making Kodachadri a significant religious and historical site.

faqs.question: What is Hidlumane Falls on the Kodachadri Trek?
faqs.answer: Hidlumane Falls is a natural waterfall on the Kodachadri Trek trail — the trail passes directly through the falls, not around it. It is one of the most memorable sections of the trek.
